source.label: Moon et al. 2019, PLOS ONE 14(9): e0216972
source.what: 1,267 adult records from two Korean emergency departments, October 2016 to September 2017

provenance.real: Taken from the record unchanged: sex, age, arrival, injury, recorded complaint, alertness, pain score, vital signs, diagnosis, the nurse's KTAS level, the expert panel's KTAS level, the cause of a nurse's error.
provenance.derived: Written by a fixed rule from one real field, named in each fact's 'from': the patient's opening words (from the recorded complaint) and the fact sheet (pain from the pain score, fever from temperature, breathlessness from breathing rate or oxygen, racing heart from pulse, faintness from blood pressure, alertness from the mental-state code).
provenance.synthetic: Not in the record: the behaviour traits, drawn at random as in the main experiment. Onset, duration, medical history and medicines are not in the published file and are left out of the fact sheet.

limits: Everyone here went to an emergency department, so there are no pharmacy or self-care cases.
The nurse saw the patient and measured blood pressure, pulse, temperature and oxygen. A form or chat gets only what the patient can say.
The right level is the Korean KTAS scale (1 to 5), not an NHS service.
21 complaints were lost in the published file (Korean text saved as question marks); those patients open with a generic line.
